The main takeaway from our work is that
the O‐antigen structure of the LPS from V. cholera O1 is not a single structure, as previously thought, but a mixture of two distinct structures.
the AB(c) and AC structures are not merely serological structures, but are also the structural bases for the serological distinction between the Ogawa and inaba O‐forms, respectively.
the Ogawa and inaba antigens of V. cholerea O1 are encoded by different sets of genes that are located on separate cosmid clones in the genome of V. cholorea O1.
